name: Business credit card points consulting
one_liner: Show business owners how to get much more value from the credit card points they already earn on spending they already do, in one paid consultation.
customer: Small business owners who put a lot of business spending on cards
offer: A one-time points strategy package delivered on a call: which cards to use, how to redeem points and how to transfer them to airline or hotel schemes
how_it_makes_money: Flat one-time fee of $875 per client
time_to_first_revenue: weeks (he learned the topic a few months before starting)
evidence: Charges $875 one-time; $231,000 in his first full year (rvOnhGzx__Q)
Made $13,000 the month he quit his job; costs about $100 in software (rvOnhGzx__Q)
Clients 'show up in my inbox every single day', no outbound sales (rvOnhGzx__Q)
risks: The UK has fewer business card and points options than the US (mainly Amex, Avios and Virgin), so there is less value per client
Inbound demand probably came from content or SEO that isn't explained in the video
Card issuers change their rules often
May need to stay clear of anything that looks like regulated financial advice

name: Simple custom apps that replace no-code tool stacks
one_liner: Use AI coding tools to build small, single-purpose apps for small businesses that would otherwise pay for expensive no-code subscriptions, then charge a monthly fee to host and run them.
customer: Small business owners and startups, often found on Upwork
offer: A custom 'stupid simple' app, such as a data entry tool, plus hosting and maintenance
how_it_makes_money: A build fee plus a monthly fee (for example $50/month instead of a $250/month no-code stack)
time_to_first_revenue: about 2 weeks ('nothing to full-time freelancer or agency in 2 weeks')
evidence: Data entry app for an auto mechanic coaching business: $50/month versus a $250/month Airtable no-code stack (tFP7wnWkX4w)
Now runs an app agency with a team of four (tFP7wnWkX4w)
risks: Lots of competition on Upwork
Ongoing support and maintenance obligations to clients
Small monthly fees take many clients to add up

name: Conversion copywriting for email lists
one_liner: Write sales emails and landing pages using the AIDA framework (attention, interest, desire, action) for businesses that already have an email list.
customer: E-commerce, SaaS and deal-site businesses with an existing list
offer: Done-for-you sales emails and sales pages
how_it_makes_money: Per-project or retainer copywriting fees (pricing not stated)
evidence: His first AppSumo email produced their first $10,000 profit day, from a list of about 50,000 (uGzNhjFJYFI)
'We write all these emails for Fortune 500 companies' (uGzNhjFJYFI)
risks: AI is pushing prices down
Needs proof of results to win clients
No pricing given in the video

name: Facebook ads for local service businesses
one_liner: Run Meta ad campaigns that generate messages and leads for local trades businesses that currently just boost posts.
customer: Local service businesses such as HVAC and tree trimming
offer: Ad setup, ad copy, testing and lead handling or CRM automation
evidence: An HVAC owner with 12 years in business had only one boosted post with no targeting (uUlU5G1Nda0)
Weak evidence: tutorial only, with no revenue figures
risks: Very crowded agency market
Clients leave when results drop
Needs ad budget and sales calls

name: AI-assisted niche Amazon KDP books
one_liner: Use research tools to find book topics with unmet demand on Amazon, then write them with AI help and publish through KDP for passive royalties.
customer: Amazon book buyers in narrow niches
evidence: Shannon makes 'thousands of dollars a month' passively from books, but he built that before AI (sDtJaQynQkA)
Admits most KDP sellers 'don't find the success' (sDtJaQynQkA)
risks: Market flooded with AI-written books
Amazon policy crackdowns
Weak evidence that AI-written books earn money

name: Niche invoicing SaaS that earns on payments
one_liner: Build free invoicing software for one industry and earn a markup on card payments processed through it.
offer: Free invoicing app with payments built in
how_it_makes_money: About 0.5% markup on top of Stripe's ~2.9% fee
evidence: Google search suggestions show demand for free invoicing software for small businesses and specific trades (uQKVxCQJPoA)
Weak evidence: an idea built live in the video, with no revenue
risks: Needs a lot of payment volume
Strong incumbents (Xero, QuickBooks)
Hard to win customers

name: Grant-funded vocational training school
one_liner: Run a trade or IT training school whose students' fees are paid by government workforce grants.
customer: US state workforce programmes (WIOA) paying for eligible students
offer: Trade and IT training plus job placement
how_it_makes_money: Grant payments of $5,000–$15,000 per student, or about $3,000 per student from the general public
evidence: Scaled one school to $2.4M in its first year on grants alone, with $0 spent on marketing (scZxo7_zLdI)
An IT school client brings in about $5M a year combined from training and placement (scZxo7_zLdI)
risks: The grant is US-specific; the UK equivalents (Skills Bootcamps, the apprenticeship levy) work differently
Heavy accreditation and compliance requirements
Hands-on, in-person delivery
